items.delivery: PK=endpoint#<endpointId> SK=delivery#<eventId> | shopId, eventId, deliveryId, type, kind (event|replay|ping), state, attempt (the number the next attempt carries), nextAttemptAt, claimedAt, claimedAtMs, cancelReason, failureReason, body (exact signed JSON, <= 256 KiB), createdAt, expiresAtEpoch
items.attempt: PK=endpoint#<endpointId> SK=attempt#<startedAtIso>#<attemptId> | attemptId, deliveryId, eventId, type, attempt, startedAt, durationMs, status (http code or null), ok, error, responseSnippet (<= 1 KiB), replay, expiresAtEpoch

accessPatterns: dashboard log: Query PK=endpoint#e AND begins_with(SK, 'attempt#') ScanIndexForward=false; the cursor is ExclusiveStartKey (startedAt, attemptId)
event detail and replay: GetItem PK=endpoint#e SK=delivery#<eventId>, re-send the stored body
claim: conditional UpdateItem on the delivery item (state, attempt); result: TransactWriteItems of the attempt item and the delivery state
reads filter expiresAtEpoch > now themselves: the TTL sweep is lazy (AS-60, AS-67)
_design.why: write-heavy append log (every attempt), read by endpoint, expiring after 30 days - no reason to bloat Postgres with it
